members.title: BNP MP Selimuzzaman's house in Gopalganj torched
members.lead: There have been incidents of attacks, vandalism, and arson at the houses of several members, including a Member of Parliament (MP) of Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) in Gopalganj. Today, Thursday, from the morning, these incidents took place by the Awami League, whose activities now banned, and Jubo League, and banned Chhatra League leaders and activists, who were holding processions, protests, and carrying local weapons in various areas of the district. At around 12 PM today, there was an attack, vandalism, and arson at the house of former district BNP president and former chairman of the district council, MH Khan Manju, on Bangabandhu Road in the city. . Earlier, at 11 AM, attacks, vandalism, and arson were carried out at the house of Gopalganj-1 constituency MP Selimuzzaman Molla and several houses of his relatives and supporters in Kashiani. According to local sources, today at around 11 AM, local leaders and activists of the Awami League and Jubo League, and banned Chhatra League gathered with a procession in Jayanagar market of Kashiani upazila. They were led by Maheshpur union Parishad (UP) chairman Lutfur Rahman. At one stage, vandalism and looting were carried out at the shops of the MP's brothers, Hafiz Molla and Rafiqul Molla. . Later, a procession was taken to Selimuzzaman Molla’s house in Shivgati village of Maheshpur Union. The attackers threw crude bombs and petrol bombs, entered the house, and carried out vandalism and arson. Attacks, vandalism, and arson were also executed at several houses of MP Selimuzzaman Molla’s relatives and neighbours. . Muksudpur upazila BNP General Secretary Tariqul Islam stated that in the morning, a group of people came with a procession and vandalised the houses of the Member of Parliament. At that time, a cocktail explosion occurred, and at one stage, the house was set on fire. members.title: BNP leader killed in Narail: 'Bring my brother back alive,' sister pleads
members.lead: "I won’t take his body. Bring my brother back alive. I took my brother to Khulna. The veins in his hands and legs were severed, his throat was slit, and he had been shot in the head," said Jyoti Khanam, struggling to speak through her tears. Pausing briefly, she said, “My beloved brother. I saw him lying lifeless before my eyes. I want justice for him.” Jyoti’s brother, Sohel Rana, general secretary of the Jatiyatabadi Samajik Sanskritik Sangstha (JASAS) in Narail’s Kalia upazila, was killed on Wednesday night. He was attacked by leaders and activists of the Awami League, whose activities are currently banned. The Prothom Alo correspondent spoke to Jyoti at Sohel Rana’s home in Boro Kalia village of Kalia upazila on Thursday morning. . Two BNP leaders, including Sohel Rana, were killed when leaders and activists of the Awami League, attacked a BNP motorcycle procession in Kalia upazila on Wednesday evening. Sohel Rana, 45, was the general secretary of the upazila unit of JASAS, while Shahinur Islam, 40, was the general secretary of the municipal unit of Jatiyatabadi Krishak Dal. Police said post-mortem examinations of the two bodies had not yet been completed. No one had been arrested in connection with the incident by 1:45pm on Thursday. The situation in Kalia municipality has remained tense since the incident. Police personnel have been patrolling intersections to maintain law and order. . Earlier in the morning, family members were seen weeping at Shahinur’s home in Mirzapur village under Kalia municipality. Neighbours, local residents and relatives were arriving at the house one after another. Some were trying to console the bereaved family. . Shahinur’s wife, Rima Khatun, said in despair, ‘Everyone will hear about the incident, but no one will feel the pain. No one will see the agony I am going through. My child has lost his father. members.title: Activities-banned Awami League activists set fire to another police station
members.lead: Leaders and activists of the Awami League, whose activities are currently banned, and its affiliated organisations attacked Muksudpur Police Station in Gopalganj, setting fire to the building and carrying out extensive vandalism. They also set fire to 10 vehicles, including a police vehicle parked inside the station. The incident took place around noon on Thursday. Tensions have been running high across Gopalganj amid the Awami League’s announced lockdown programme. Attacks, vandalism, looting and arson have been reported in different parts of the district in connection with the programme. Several videos showing the attack, vandalism and arson at Muksudpur Police Station have also circulated on Facebook. In one video, leaders and activists of the Awami League and its affiliated organisations are seen taking selfies and recording videos after setting fire to the police station. At one point, a man is heard saying, ‘Come on, chant Joy Bangla. ... This is Muksudpur Police Station! Muksudpur Police Station has been made Joy Bangla.’ The video also shows the activists celebrating after vandalising and setting fire to the police station. . Another video shows several hundred leaders and activists of the banned Awami League and its affiliated organisations entering the police station and setting fire to all the cars and motorcycles parked on the premises. They are also seen vandalising every room in the building and setting fire to both the ground and first floors. .Operations at Tungipara police station suspended after vandalism, arson. Two hours after the incident, the fire was still burning. No firefighters or anyone else were seen attempting to extinguish it. Speaking to several local residents and journalists, it was learnt that no police personnel had been present at the Muksudpur police station building since Wednesday evening. members.title: Train services suspended in Gopalganj and adjoining routes
members.lead: Train services in Gopalganj have been suspended amid arson attacks on police stations and houses of a local member of parliament, as well as demonstrations by the Awami League, whose activities have been banned. Train services to Khulna via Gopalganj have also been suspended. The suspended services include intercity, commuter and local trains. Four trains in total have been taken out of service. These trains used to make multiple trips a day. Railway sources said the Ruposhi Bangla Express travels from Khulna to Dhaka in the morning. It then runs from Dhaka to Benapole via Gopalganj before returning to Khulna from Benapole as an intercity train. .Activities-banned Awami League holds protest march in Gopalganj with machetes, hockey sticks. On Wednesday, the train arrived in Dhaka from Khulna but could not proceed beyond Bhanga station in Faridpur on its way to Benapole. Its journey was subsequently suspended. The train did not operate today, Thursday. Railway officials said there were problems in Narail as well as Gopalganj. For this reason, the train service has been suspended. The Tungipara Express runs between Chapainawabganj and Tungipara in Gopalganj via Pabna and Rajbari. Yesterday, the train could not proceed beyond Kalukhali in Rajbari. It was then sent back to Chapainawabganj from Kalukhali. The authorities have decided to operate the train only between Chapainawabganj and Kalukhali from today. .BNP MP Selimuzzaman's house in Gopalganj torched. Besides, the ‘Abhijatri’ commuter train operating between Dhaka and Gopalganj has also been suspended, railway sources said. The train makes one trip from Dhaka and one return trip each day. It was primarily introduced to allow passengers to travel to and from Gopalganj within the same day. Yesterday, the train left Dhaka but got stuck after reaching Bhanga. members.title: Security tightened as 74 vehicles set on fire, crude bombs explode at 74 spots in 12 days
members.lead: A series of acts of sabotage have taken place in different parts of the country surrounding the lockdown programme announced by the Awami League, whose activities are currently banned. Incidents include crude bomb explosions, arson attacks on moving and parked vehicles, and fires at government and privately owned establishments. According to police data, crude bombs exploded at 78 locations between 7 and 18 November, while 74 vehicles were set on fire over the 12 days. A total of 38 cases have been filed across the country in connection with these incidents. Police have so far arrested 63 people in these cases. . According to data provided by the police, three police establishments were also set on fire and vandalised during this period. In addition, there were reports of arson attacks on 18 vehicles, crude bomb explosions at two establishments and one vehicle damaged in a crude bomb explosion. . Meanwhile, incidents of arson and sabotage involving government and private establishments and vehicles have been reported in 16 districts across the country today, Thursday, including an attack on the house of a BNP member of parliament (MP) in Gopalganj. The incidents took place between Wednesday night and Thursday noon. The districts are Gopalganj, Chattogram, Gazipur, Natore, Mymensingh, Tangail, Kishoreganj, Chandpur, Narayanganj, Netrakona, Rajshahi, Panchagarh, Rangpur, Pabna, Sunamganj and Sylhet. . Sources concerned said the perpetrators were targeting KIPs (key point installations). They have plans to launch further attacks on police stations and other important state installations in the coming days. Information has also emerged about plans to disrupt road and waterway communications. In this situation, security has been strengthened at key state installations, police said.
